settings.text: 6 reasons cooks are switching to a thermometer
"Roasting and grilling should always be this stress-free." Wired
It tells you when your food will be done, not just how hot it is right now.

• Live countdown to the minute it's done
  • Plans for resting, so it never overshoots
  • 8 sensors find the true center for you

intro.name: Intro

settings.text:
Every cook knows the moment. Guests are hungry, the roast looks done, and you're stabbing it with a thermometer for the fourth time, watching the juices run out of every hole. A single reading tells you where the meat is right now. It can't tell you when dinner will be ready, and if you hit the wrong spot it can't even tell you that.

The Combustion Predictive Thermometer was built to answer the question cooks actually ask: how long until it's done? It was co-designed by Chris Young, a former Modernist Cuisine chef, and J. Kenji López-Alt calls it game-changing. Here are six reasons it's replacing the old probe in kitchens and on grills.

settings.text: It tells you when dinner will be ready, to the minute

Most thermometers report a number. The Predictive Thermometer reads how fast heat is moving through your food and counts down to the moment it reaches your target. Side dishes, plating and guests all line up with a real ETA instead of a guess.

It even accounts for carryover cooking, so you can pull a steak or roast before it overshoots and let it rest up to the perfect temperature.
Eight sensors mean you can't miss the center

A single-point probe is only as good as where you stick it. Combustion's probe carries eight sensors along its length, and its TrueCore feature automatically tracks the coolest one: the true center of whatever you're cooking.
Insert it once. No repositioning, no second-guessing.
SafeCook takes the fear out of chicken and pork

Food safety isn't only about one temperature. It's about how long food stays at temperature. SafeCook tracks that for you and alerts you the moment your food is safe to eat, so you stop overcooking "just to be safe" and serve chicken that's still juicy and tender.
Truly wireless, from oven to smoker to rotisserie

There's no cable to pinch in the oven door and nothing to dangle off the grill. The probe works in the oven, on the grill, in a smoker, a pan or a water bath, even on a spinning rotisserie.

Watch it on the free Combustion app (iOS, Android, macOS and watchOS) or glance at the optional WiFi Display, no phone needed. With WiFi you can check in from anywhere.
It's built by people obsessed with cooking science

Combustion was co-founded by Chris Young, a chef and author who helped create Modernist Cuisine. The prediction engine comes from years of heat-transfer modeling, not a lookup table. That's why serious cooks trust it, and why J. Kenji López-Alt partners with the brand.
Every Predictive Thermometer comes with a two-year warranty and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Cook with it through the holidays. If it doesn't change how you cook, send it back.

settings.heading: Does it work on a grill or smoker?

settings.text: Yes. The probe is fully wireless and made for ovens, grills, smokers, rotisseries, pans and sous vide. Leave it in for the whole cook.

settings.heading: How is "predictive" different from a timer?

settings.text: A timer guesses from a recipe. The Predictive Thermometer measures how your specific food is heating right now and updates the countdown as conditions change.

settings.heading: What if it's not for me?

settings.text: You have 30 days to return it for a full refund, and a two-year warranty after that.
